Getting Sick

Oxford Read and Discover · Level 2 · Your Body · Pages 16–17

🔒 New Words 1 · Listen & Fill 2 · Write 3 · Present 4 · Mind Map

★ New Words

🔒 This part is for the teacher.

Teach these words before the listening task. Press 🔊 to hear the word (American English). Show the picture, read the meaning, then read the example.

sick

adjective

Not well. Your body feels bad.

“Germs can make you sick.”

germ

noun

A very, very small thing that can make you sick.

“Germs can get in your body.”

finger

noun

One of the five parts at the end of your hand.

“Germs can get in your mouth from your fingers.”

cut

noun

A small open line in your skin.

“Germs get in when you get a cut.”

soap

noun

You use it with water to wash.

“Wash your hands with soap and water.”

toilet

noun

The place in the bathroom where you go to pee.

“Wash your hands after you go to the toilet.”

animal

noun

A living thing like a dog or a cat.

“Wash your hands after you touch animals.”

sneeze

noun

Air that comes out of your nose fast: “Achoo!”

“There are germs in a sneeze.”

tissue

noun

A soft paper for your nose.

“Catch sneezes in a tissue.”

wastebasket

noun

A small bin for trash.

“Throw the tissue in a wastebasket.”

2 Write a Summary

Write about germs and getting sick in your own words. Write 15 words or more. Then you can see my example.

💡 Answer these questions

  1. What are germs?
  2. How do germs get in your body?
  3. How can you get germs off your fingers?
  4. When do you wash your hands?
  5. Where are there germs?
  6. What do you do when you sneeze?

✏️ Start like this

  • Germs are …
  • Germs get in my body when …
  • I wash my hands with …
  • I wash my hands after …
  • There are germs in …
  • When I sneeze, I …
0 / 15 words

⭐ Example Summary

Germs are things that can make me sick. Germs get in my body when I breathe and eat, and from my fingers. They can get in a cut in my skin, too. I wash my hands with soap and water before I eat, after I go to the toilet, after I touch animals, and after I play outside. There are germs in a sneeze, so I catch sneezes in a tissue and throw it in a wastebasket.

3 Presentation Script

Read the script. Practise it. Then present to your class!

Hello!Start

Good morning, everyone! My name is ________. Today I want to talk about germs and getting sick.

Look at this picture. These are germs! They are very, very small.

👉 Show the germs picture.
Part 1Germs

Do you get sick? Germs are things that can make us sick.

Germs can get in our body when we breathe and when we eat. They can get in our mouth from our fingers, too.

👉 Wiggle your fingers. Point to your mouth.
Part 2A cut

Some germs get in our body when we get a cut in our skin.

👉 Point to your arm.
Part 3Wash hands

We wash our hands with soap and water to get germs off our fingers.

👉 Pretend to wash your hands.
Part 4When?

We wash our hands when it’s time to eat, after we go to the toilet, after we touch animals, and after we play outside.

Question for you: When do you wash your hands? (Wait for answers.)

👉 Count on your fingers: 1, 2, 3, 4. Then ask the class.
Part 5Sneeze

Stop germs! There are germs in a sneeze. We catch sneezes in a tissue. Then we throw the tissue in a wastebasket.

👉 Pretend to sneeze into a tissue: “Achoo!”
The EndFinish

Remember: wash your hands and catch your sneezes. Let’s stop germs!

Thank you for listening! Do you have any questions?

👉 Smile and say “Thank you!”

🌟 Presentation Tips

  • Speak slowly and loudly.
  • Look at your friends, not only at the paper.
  • Point to the pictures when you talk.
  • Smile! 😊
